text: The Krishna Paksha (dark fortnight) that comes after Bhadrapada Purnima is called Mahalaya Paksha or Pitru Paksha.
According to this year's Telugu Panchangam, Pitru Paksha will be from September 27 to October 10.
The last day is Mahalaya Amavasya — Sarva Pitru Amavasya.
Not just the parents who gave us birth, but also their previous generations, and generations before them; it is because of that lineage that we exist today.
Pitru Paksha is the period allocated by Sanatanam to specially remember them and express gratitude.
What is done on these days?
According to family tradition, Shraddha, Tarpanam, and Pinda Pradanam are performed on the Tithi (lunar day) when ancestors passed away.
Those who cannot perform these can also remember their ancestors.
They can perform Annadanam (food donation) or other donations in their name.
Pitru Paksha is not an inauspicious period.
Because these days are dedicated to remembering ancestors, traditionally new auspicious events like weddings and housewarmings are not started during this time.
Sanatanam, which worships the divine, also considered expressing gratitude to our roots as Dharma.
Note: There is a tradition of performing Purnima Shraddha on Bhadrapada Purnima on September 26.
The Pitru Paksha Krishna Paksha Tithis begin with Padyami on September 27.
The method of Pitru Karmas may vary depending on family, region, and tradition.
